newsitem.title: INDIA: Poll says most Indians think PM should step down.
newsitem.headline: Poll says most Indians think PM should step down.

text.p: A leading opinion poll said on Sunday most Indians want Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda to quit and predicted major gains for his right-wing Hindu nationalist rivals if widely discussed mid-term elections are held soon.

The poll published by India Today news magazine said Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left United Front alliance and its reluctant supporter, the Congress party, would lose some seats in parliament in the event of snap polls.

A senior Congress leader, however, told Reuters on Sunday his party has no plans to withdraw its make-or-break support for the United Front's minority rule during the parliament's budget session due to start on February 20.

"The Congress does not have the required strength to form its own government," former Congress minister Rajesh Pilot said. "There are no plans to force an election now. And that would become inevitable if we withdraw support to Deve Gowda."
The India Today poll, based on a survey of 12,832 registered voters, said 62 percent of respondents feel Deve Gowda should be replaced while 27 percent said he should stay in his post.
But the poll found the 63-year-old farmer-turned-politician enjoys a largely favorable public image.
While 60 percent said he was "efficient", 29 percent found him to be a "bungler". Fifty-eight percent said he was "honest" and 21 percent said he was "corrupt".
Deve Gowda is often caricatured by newspaper cartoonists as a sleepy, non-descript regional leader from the backwaters of the southern state of Karnataka.
But 74 percent of the respondents said he was "clever", 56 percent described him as a "visionary", and 56 percent said he was "trustworthy". However, 14 percent said he was "foolish".

The main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which controls 194 parliamentary seats following inconclusive general elections in May last year, is expected to increase its tally to 240 in snap elections, the poll said.

The United Front was expected to lose nine of the 179 seats its won in May. The Congress, which suffered its worst-ever defeat in the elections, was expected to fall further to 115 from the 139 seats it won last year.
The poll said only nine percent favoured Deve Gowda to remain as prime minister, but did not award anyone else a comfortable lead.

Some 29 percent favoured the BJP's Atal Behari Vajpayee. Eight percent chose Sonia Gandhi, the Italian-born widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, who has so far kept out of politics since Gandhi's assassination in 1991.
